source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
3.3V rail (AXP2101 DCDC1, 2A) — primary power source when power board is connected:
\- ESP32-S3 module
\- INA219
\- All I2C sensors (SCD41, BME280, ENS160) via sensor board
\- I2C display
\- TTP223, AM312 PIR

5V rail (MT3608 boost, 500mA) — controlled by ESP32 GPIO3:
\- SPS30 particulate sensor
\- ZE08-CH2O formaldehyde sensor
\- SK6812 LEDs (if wired to 5V — depends on version)

3.3V rail (ME6211A LDO, 1A) — only active when USB-C on main board connected WITHOUT power board:
\- Same 3.3V rail as above — Schottky diode OR-ing means whichever source is present wins. Used for standalone programming.

Battery (3.7–4.2V) — feeds AXP2101 which then feeds everything above.

Simple rule: in normal operation AXP2101 powers everything. The LDO only kicks in when programming without the power board connected.

value_updates.activation_condition: main-board USB-C connected without the power board
value_updates.source_selection: Schottky diode OR-ing with the AXP2101 DCDC1 supply

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
A few things to check on the schematic:
1\. LD1117S33CTR is 800mA — we specified 1A. Is that enough for standalone USB mode?
2\. Shunt resistors are 0.01Ω — was that intentional? Gives 4mA resolution vs 0.4mA with 0.1Ω. 3. IRLML2402 for the SK6812 level shift — does it have a pull-up on the 5V side? SK6812 timing is tight (~300ns), want to make sure the edges are fast enough. Would 74AHCT1G125 be safer?

ambiguity.description: The schematic uses an 800mA regulator despite the specified 1A standalone-USB capacity, and the client asks whether 800mA is sufficient.

The integrated board's 3.3V rail starts successfully; the concrete failure reported here is native USB enumeration.
